statement: Global data-centre electricity use in 2027 is below the IEA's 2025 base-case projection for 2027 (IEA; 2028 release)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable in 2023: the reference projection (IEA 2025 base case) did not exist. 2023 context: IEA put 2022 data-centre use at 240-340 TWh (1-1.3% of global electricity, excl. crypto) and expected moderate growth; a peer-reviewed commentary estimated AI servers alone could use 85-134 TWh/yr by 2027.

items.summary: International energy agency tracking report: global data-centre electricity use in 2022 was an estimated 240-340 TWh (about 1-1.3% of global final electricity demand, excluding ~110 TWh crypto mining); large-data-centre use has grown 20-40% a year, but overall use was expected to grow only moderately over the next few years.
items.detail: IEA, 'Tracking Data Centres and Data Transmission Networks' (2023 edition, page verified via web_extract this run; the publication day is not shown in the extracted text - 2023-07-11 is approximate, from the IEA tracking-report cycle).

items.summary: Peer-reviewed commentary: if the dominant AI-server vendor ships ~1.5 million AI servers by 2027, they could draw 9.75-15.3 GW and consume 85.4-134.0 TWh a year at full utilisation, versus ~5.7-8.9 TWh for 2023 shipments; cautions against both extreme scenarios.
items.detail: Alex de Vries, 'The growing energy footprint of artificial intelligence', Joule 7(10), October 2023 (verified via web_extract this run; online date 2023-10-10 not shown in extracted text, approximate). Based on NVIDIA server shipment projections.

items.summary: The benchmark the indicator uses (the agency's 2025 base-case projection for 2027) had not been published by the end of the phase.
items.detail: IEA's dedicated AI-and-energy base case appeared in 2025 (excluded under the as-of rule). Reference page opened this run: IEA data-centre tracking page (2023 edition).
